title: The row of icon previews stays up when you pick nothing
goal: While you are drawing an icon, a row of small previews at the top left of the canvas shows it at the sizes it will really be used. Click an empty part of the canvas, or press Escape, and the whole row vanishes, because it only knows which icon to show from whatever is selected. Deselecting is the ordinary way to stand back and look at what you have drawn, and it is exactly the moment the previews are worth most. Keep them up.
acceptance: Draw inside an icon frame, then click empty canvas or press Escape: the previews row is still there and still shows that icon
With the pointer over a different icon frame and nothing picked, the row shows that frame's icon, the same way the Width row already decides
A document with no icon frame in it still draws no previews and pays nothing for them
A scripted walk covers deselecting with an icon frame open, so this cannot come back
The try path: New Frame, pick an icon size, draw a shape in it, press Escape. Ships in Next behind next-icon-previews, which is on by default
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock-free question here was what the row should show when NOTHING is picked and the pointer is over neither an icon nor anything else, which is exactly the state clicking empty canvas leaves you in. A pointer-only fallback (the Width row's rule as written) would have left the bug alive for the click, since the click puts the pointer on bare canvas. So the rule is picked, then pointer, then the last icon either of them named, with the last part checked against the document on every read rather than expiring - an icon that has been deleted, or one that was never an icon frame, is dropped. Shortest version that delivers it: one pure function in PhotonzCore and one remembered id on EditorState.

left rough: merely passing the pointer over a second icon frame moves the row onto it and it stays there once the pointer moves off. Deliberate, and inherited from the Width row's shipped rule (iconFrameSize(picked:pointerIn:)) rather than a second answer invented here; the audit asks the user whether the row should instead stick to the icon you last drew in. No open task covers it and it is a judgment call rather than a defect, so it is here rather than filed.

left rough: at high zoom the frame's own name chip sits immediately right of the previews card in the top left corner, and now that the card stays up the two are adjacent much more of the time (see queue/audits/2026-09-19-icon-previews-stay-up-1.png). They do not overlap in any capture taken here, so it is a crowding question rather than a bug; the audit asks about it.

New playtest step kind expectIconPreviews (sides, or absent:true): reads the editor's own strip and fails with which icon it is speaking for and which icon frames the document holds. Forced under a lock on 2026-09-19 it ran clean through all 77 steps, so it was added to PlaytestLockSafety.stepsThatSurviveALock with that evidence written into the doc comment, and the walk now runs unforced on a locked Mac (lockSafe true, 6 real window captures).
